title: Pre-Training and Prompting for Few-Shot Node Classification on Text-Attributed Graphs

problem.claim: Few-shot node classification on text-attributed graphs must classify nodes associated with raw text.

gap.claim: Traditional few-shot node classification methods train on pre-processed node features without considering raw text, and their performance depends heavily on feature preprocessing.

contributions.claim: P2TAG is a framework for few-shot node classification on text-attributed graphs that combines graph pre-training and prompting.
P2TAG pre-trains a language model and graph neural network on text-attributed graphs using self-supervised loss, adapting masked language modeling to the framework.
P2TAG uses a mixed prompt method for few-shot node classification that jointly considers text and graph information.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on six real-world text-attributed graphs, including paper citation and product co-purchasing networks.
The authors report that P2TAG outperforms existing graph few-shot learning methods on the evaluated datasets by 18.98% to 32.14%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Text-attributed graphs associate raw text with each node and are presented as an important real-world graph data type.
Existing few-shot node classification methods use pre-processed node features, omit raw texts, and depend on feature preprocessing choices.
The paper proposes P2TAG, which pre-trains language and graph models with self-supervision, adapts masked language modeling, and applies mixed prompting over text and graph information.
The authors evaluate P2TAG on six real-world text-attributed graphs and report improvements over existing graph few-shot learning methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six datasets, baselines, task splits, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not explain the model architecture, prompting procedure, or self-supervised losses beyond masked language modeling adaptation.
The reported improvement range lacks per-dataset results and uncertainty estimates.
